## Overview

**Core question:** does the implementation correctly downsample a multisample color attachment into a single-sample resolve attachment across all render-pass styles, every supported color format, and every sample-mask pattern?

This page covers the `multisample_resolve` test family implemented in [`vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp`](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp). The family lives under `renderpasses.<rendering_type>.suballocation.multisample_resolve` and is registered once per rendering path: `renderpass1`, `renderpass2`, and `dynamic_rendering`.

The core test idea is:

- Render a solid color into a multisample color attachment, controlling which sample locations are written via `gl_SampleMask`.
- Let the implementation resolve that attachment into a single-sample image.
- Copy the single-sample image back to host memory and check that the resolved value matches what the resolve rule (average for float/fixed-point, sample zero for integer) requires.

The page explains the resolve mechanism the tests exercise, the matrix of formats and sample counts, the three matrix test shapes (`RESOLVE`, `MAX_ATTACHMENTS`, `COMPATIBILITY`), the separately registered `mixed_sample_count_subpasses` case that switches sample counts between subpasses, how each case is verified, and what a failure implies.

## Background Knowledge

- **Multisample resolve.** A multisample color attachment stores one value per sample location per pixel. A resolve operation combines those per-sample values into a single value per pixel and writes it to a single-sample (resolve) attachment. The Vulkan spec defines two resolve modes relevant here: `VK_RESOLVE_MODE_AVERAGE_BIT` averages the sample values (used for floating-point and fixed-point color formats), and `VK_RESOLVE_MODE_SAMPLE_ZERO_BIT` takes the value of sample zero (used for integer color formats, where averaging is not defined). This mode split drives most of the test design.
- **`gl_SampleMask`.** A fragment-shader output mask that controls which sample locations in the covered pixel receive the fragment's output. By cycling every possible mask value for a given sample count, the tests can distinguish "resolve picked sample zero" from "resolve averaged" from "resolve is inconsistent," because each mask pattern produces a known mix of written and unwritten samples.
- **Render pass styles exercised.** The same logic is exercised through `VkRenderPass` (legacy, `renderpass1`), `VkRenderPass2` via `VK_KHR_create_renderpass2`, and dynamic rendering via `VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering` (with `VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering_local_read` for the max-attachments shape). The resolve attachment is bound as a `pResolveAttachments` entry in legacy/`renderpass2`, or as `pResolveImageView`/`resolveMode` in dynamic rendering.
- **Subpass dependency granularity.** A subpass dependency orders work between two subpasses over the whole render area, or only per pixel region when it carries `VK_DEPENDENCY_BY_REGION_BIT`. Under by-region ordering two subpasses may overlap over different parts of the same attachment as long as each individual pixel is ordered. Later reasoning about a case where one subpass resolves an attachment and a following subpass renders into that same attachment depends on this distinction, because a mistake there can show up in one region of the image instead of everywhere.

## Registration Hierarchy

```text
renderpasses.renderpass1.suballocation.multisample_resolve
├── layers_3
├── layers_6
└── mixed_sample_count
```

The representative root is `renderpasses.renderpass1.suballocation.multisample_resolve`. In addition to the children shown above, the root also directly contains 50 format-named test families (for example `r8g8b8a8_unorm`, `r16_sfloat`), each holding the `samples_<N>`, `samples_<N>_baseLayer1`, `samples_<N>_resolve_level_<L>`, `max_attachments_<P>_samples_<N>`, and `compatibility_samples_<N>` test case leaves described in `## Behavior Parameters`. The full format list is given in `## Parameter Dimensions and Observed Values`.

The `mixed_sample_count` child is not part of that matrix. It is a fixed group holding the single `mixed_sample_count_subpasses` test case leaf, created in [`createRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests`](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3943-L3948) only when the group's rendering type is not dynamic rendering, which is why the leaf appears in mustpass under `renderpass1` and `renderpass2` (and the two `dEQP-VKSC` equivalents) but never under `dynamic_rendering`.

The matrix shapes are also registered under `renderpass2` and `dynamic_rendering` (both primary and secondary command buffer variants, plus graphics pipeline library) and are generated by the same [`initTests`](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3761) loop.

|-----------|-------------------|----------------------|----------|
| Color formats | 50 `VkFormat` values (color-attachment capable, including `VK_FORMAT_A8_UNORM_KHR`) | Each format selects the resolve mode (`AVERAGE` for float/fixed-point, `SAMPLE_ZERO` for integer) and the channel class used for verification. | [formats array](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3763-L3816) |
| Sample counts | `2`, `4`, `8` | Number of samples per pixel; determines the mask bit-width (`2^N` patterns) and the expected average for float/fixed-point formats. | [sampleCounts](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3817) |
| Layer counts | `1`, `3`, `6` | Array layers in the color and resolve images; `>1` requires geometry shader for layered rendering. | [layerCounts](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3818) |
| Resolve levels | `2`, `3`, `4` | Mip level resolved into, when the single-sample image is mipmapped (`RESOLVE` family only, monolithic pipeline). | [resolveLevels](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3819) |
| Max attachment counts | `4`, `8`, `16` (powers of two) | Number of simultaneous color attachments for the `MAX_ATTACHMENTS` shape. | [attachment loop](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3893-L3907) |

The `mixed_sample_count_subpasses` case is not generated from this matrix. It fixes one format (`VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM`), one 4x multisample color attachment, one 1x resolve attachment, one array layer, and a 256x256 render extent ([image setup](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3320-L3355)), so it adds no new format, sample-count, or layer values to the table above.

## Behavior Parameters

The primary behavioral axis is the `TestType` enum value, which selects one of three distinct test shapes sharing the same format/sample/layer matrix. Each shape is a separate test case leaf family registered under `<formatName>` (or `<formatName>` under `layers_<N>`). A second axis, documented after the three matrix shapes, is the `mixed_sample_count_subpasses` test case, which is registered outside that matrix.

### RESOLVE: basic and resolve-variant resolve tests

`RESOLVE` is the main shape. Each registered test case renders a solid color into one or more multisample color attachments and lets the implementation resolve them, then checks the resolved single-sample result.

The [`iterate`](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L1369) method cycles `m_sampleMask` from `0` up to `2^N - 1` (the full mask). On every step it clears the attachments to a known clear value, draws a full-screen quad whose fragment shader writes a render value only to the sample locations enabled by the current mask, then resolves, copies back, and verifies. The shader output and resolve mode are both deterministic for a given mask, so each mask step has a predictable expected result.

Three `RESOLVE` variants extend the basic case:

- **Basic**: `samples_<N>`, single layer (`baseLayer 0`), resolve into mip level 0. The default `TestConfig` uses 4 attachments at 32×32.
- **Base layer offset**: `samples_<N>_baseLayer1`, same as basic but `baseLayer = 1`, so verification reads from a non-zero array layer. Monolithic pipeline only. ([source](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3857-L3864))
- **Resolve level**: `samples_<N>_resolve_level_<L>` for `L` in {2, 3, 4}, the single-sample image is a mipmap chain and the resolve targets mip level `L` (the single-sample image is allocated larger and the view bound at that level). Monolithic pipeline only. ([source](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3866-L3881))

The fragment shader for `RESOLVE` writes a per-format-channel-class constant (`255`/`127` for integer, `1.0` for float/fixed-point) into each color output, gated by `gl_SampleMask[0]` read from a push constant. The shader itself is trivial; the behavior under test is the resolve operation, not shader logic.

### MAX_ATTACHMENTS: many-attachment, two-subpass stress

`MAX_ATTACHMENTS` tests whether the implementation can resolve a large number of color attachments simultaneously and feed the resolved images through a second subpass as input attachments. The test case leaves are `max_attachments_<P>_samples_<N>` for `P` in {4, 8, 16}.

The structure is two subpasses ([instance](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L1833)):

- Subpass 0 writes a fixed per-format color into `attachmentCount` multisample color attachments, each with a resolve attachment.
- Subpass 1 binds all `attachmentCount` resolved single-sample images as input attachments and writes `attachmentCount/2` output color attachments; each output `i` combines resolved inputs `i` and `i + attachmentCount/2` (`subpassLoad(i)*0.5 + subpassLoad(partner)*0.25` for float, integer division for integer formats).

Verification compares the `attachmentCount/2` output attachments of subpass 1 against a per-format reference (`(0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.75)` linear for float/fixed-point; scaled integer equivalents) within a format-dependent threshold. The input-attachment read in subpass 1 reads the resolved single-sample image, so a correct result depends on both resolve correctness and input-attachment/local-read correctness.

This shape is registered only when the secondary-command-buffer configuration matches the "completely contains dynamic renderpass" flag, so the same test set is shared across rendering paths. Dynamic rendering additionally requires `VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering_local_read`.

### COMPATIBILITY: render pass compatibility with resolve

`COMPATIBILITY` verifies that a framebuffer and pipeline created against one render pass remain valid and resolve correctly when the draw is submitted against a spec-compatible render pass. The test case leaves are `compatibility_samples_<N>`.

The instance builds two compatible render passes ([source](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L1533)): `m_renderPass`, whose resolve attachment is referenced as `VK_ATTACHMENT_UNUSED`, and `m_renderPassCompatible`, whose resolve attachment is actually used. The framebuffer and pipeline are created against the unused-resolve pass, but the draw is submitted against the used-resolve pass ([submit](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L757)); the test then verifies the resolved output is correct. The compatibility property under test is that objects created against one render pass remain valid and behave correctly when used with the spec-compatible partner. It is excluded from dynamic rendering because dynamic rendering has no render-pass-compatibility concept.

The shapes above all keep one sample count for the whole render pass. The remaining case changes the sample count of the work that touches an attachment between subpasses of the same render pass.

### mixed_sample_count_subpasses — resolve followed by a 1x subpass on the same image

This case asks whether data that a 4x subpass resolved into a single-sample attachment survives unchanged when a later subpass of the same render pass renders into that very attachment at 1 sample per pixel.

The test compares itself against a reference instead of against a host-side expected color. Both render passes use the same two attachments: attachment 0 is a 4x `VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM` transient color attachment, attachment 1 is the 1x resolve target ([reference pass](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3137-L3172), [test pass](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3175-L3219)):

- The reference pass has a single subpass that renders at 4x with a scissor limited to the left half and resolves into the reference image.
- The test pass repeats exactly that 4x draw and resolve in subpass 0, then `vkCmdNextSubpass` and renders the other triangle at 1x with a scissor limited to the right half, this time using the 1x attachment as an ordinary color attachment with no resolve. The subpass-to-subpass dependency carries `VK_DEPENDENCY_BY_REGION_BIT`.
- A third, single-attachment render pass records right after the test pass in the same command buffer. Its fragment shader `texelFetch`es the test image and the reference image, writes red when their RGB distance exceeds `0.10`, green otherwise, and discards where both still hold the clear color. Its vertex stage only emits the left triangle, so the comparison covers the half of the image that came out of the resolve and deliberately ignores the 1x output ([comparison shader](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3100-L3104)).

So a pass means the resolve result was bit-comparable to the single-subpass reference; the case is unrelated to format variety or resolve-mode selection because the format is fixed unsigned fixed-point, where the implicit resolve averages the samples.

## Shader Analysis

### Representative Shader Walkthrough 1

#### Parameter Values Chosen

Representative path:

```text
dEQP-VK.renderpasses.renderpass1.suballocation.multisample_resolve.r8g8b8a8_unorm.samples_4
```

| Parameter choice | Meaning in this representative case |
|------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `renderpass1` | Uses the legacy render-pass path. The fragment shader is shared with the `renderpass2` and dynamic-rendering paths; only host-side render-pass construction changes. |
| `r8g8b8a8_unorm` | Selects the unsigned fixed-point generator branch, so each of the four color outputs is a floating-point `vec4` set to `1.0`. The attachments are cleared to `0.0` before each draw. |
| `samples_4` | Uses four samples per pixel. The host iterates all 16 four-bit sample masks through the fragment-stage push constant. |
| Basic `RESOLVE`, 4 attachments | The default `TestConfig` emits four color outputs and resolves each multisample attachment into its paired single-sample attachment. |

#### Purpose

This fragment shader supplies the controlled per-sample input for the fixed-function resolve test. It writes white to the sample locations selected by the host-provided mask, allowing the host to check that four-sample unsigned fixed-point resolve produces the expected average of written white and cleared black samples.

#### Structural Design

| Phase | Shader operation | Role in the test |
|-------|------------------|------------------|
| Runtime control | Load the 32-bit `sampleMask` push constant and assign it to `gl_SampleMask[0]`. | Select exactly which of the four sample locations receive the fragment outputs during this draw. |
| Known-value generation | Write `vec4(1.0)` to color locations 0 through 3. | Give every enabled sample and attachment the same known render value; disabled samples retain the `vec4(0.0)` clear value. |
| Fixed-function resolve | No resolve instruction appears in the shader. | At subpass end, Vulkan resolves each four-sample attachment into its paired single-sample attachment; host verification checks the resulting average. |

#### Shader Code

```glsl
#version 450

/// The fragment-stage push-constant range is four bytes. The host updates
/// sampleMask before every draw while cycling all 16 masks for 4x MSAA.
layout(push_constant) uniform PushConstant {
    highp uint sampleMask;
} pushConstants;

/// The basic RESOLVE configuration has four R8G8B8A8_UNORM color attachments.
/// Each output writes the same known value so attachment-to-resolve routing can
/// be checked independently of shader arithmetic.
layout(location = 0) out vec4 o_color0;
layout(location = 1) out vec4 o_color1;
layout(location = 2) out vec4 o_color2;
layout(location = 3) out vec4 o_color3;

void main (void)
{
    /// Enable only the sample locations selected by the current host mask.
    gl_SampleMask[0] = int(pushConstants.sampleMask);

    /// Enabled samples become white; disabled samples keep the black clear value.
    o_color0 = vec4(1.0);
    o_color1 = vec4(1.0);
    o_color2 = vec4(1.0);
    o_color3 = vec4(1.0);
}
```

#### Additional Info

- The pipeline layout exposes exactly one four-byte push-constant range to the fragment stage, and `drawCommands` pushes the current `m_sampleMask` immediately before drawing six vertices [pipeline layout](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L1665-L1680), [draw commands](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L697-L710).
- The shared vertex shader procedurally emits a full-screen quad from `gl_VertexIndex`; it has no resources and does not vary with format, sample count, or resolve mode [vertex generation](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L2813-L2822).
- Resolve itself is fixed-function behavior. The shader deliberately contains no sampling or averaging operation; its only tested-data contribution is the known value and coverage mask consumed by the attachment resolve.

#### Parameter Variation Summary

| Parameter dimension | Shader-level variation from this shader | Evidence |
|---------------------|-----------------------------------------|----------|
| Format channel class | Unsigned integer formats use `uvec4(255)`, signed integer formats use `ivec4(127)`, and floating/fixed-point formats use `vec4(1.0)`. | [channel-class specialization](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L2872-L2890) |
| Attachment count | Basic `RESOLVE` emits four output declarations and stores; `COMPATIBILITY` emits one. The generator creates one output at each location from zero through `attachmentCount - 1`. | [output generation loop](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L2896-L2908), [registered configurations](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3167-L3169) |
| Sample count | The fragment source is unchanged for 2x, 4x, and 8x MSAA. The host changes the rasterization sample count and cycles a correspondingly wider runtime mask. | [sample-count registration](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3817-L3847), [mask iteration](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L1369-L1531) |
| Layer count | The fragment source stays unchanged. Layer counts 3 and 6 add a geometry shader that broadcasts each triangle and assigns `gl_Layer`. | [geometry-shader branch](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L2824-L2854) |
| `MAX_ATTACHMENTS` test type | This shape replaces the mask-controlled fragment shader with two generated fragment stages: the first writes a format-specific constant to 4, 8, or 16 attachments, and the second combines pairs of resolved input attachments. | [max-attachments shader generation](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L2910-L2991) |

## Runtime Execution and Result Checking

Each `RESOLVE` test case instance owns its own multisample images, single-sample (resolve) images, render pass, framebuffer, pipeline, and host-visible readback buffers ([constructor](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L659-L695)).

Per mask step:

- `[host]` clear all color attachments to the format-specific clear value (`getClearValue`): `0` for unsigned fixed-point/integer, `-1` for signed fixed-point/float, `-128` for signed integer.
- `[device]` draw a full-screen quad (6 vertices, generated procedurally in the vertex shader) writing the render value into the samples selected by the current `m_sampleMask`.
- `[device]` resolve into the single-sample attachment(s) at end of subpass / end of dynamic rendering.
- `[host]` transition the single-sample image to `TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL`, copy to host-visible buffer, invalidate mapped memory.
- `[host]` verify per-pixel against the expected resolved result for that mask.

The `MAX_ATTACHMENTS` instance runs once (no mask cycling), executing two subpasses and copying all `attachmentCount/2` output attachments back.

Final pass/fail is decided host-side by [`verify`](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L1009) for `RESOLVE`/`COMPATIBILITY` and [`MaxAttachmenstsRenderPassTestInstance::verify`](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L2264) for `MAX_ATTACHMENTS`. Failures are collected in a `tcu::ResultCollector` and the aggregate status is returned when the full mask range has been exercised.

## Failure Meaning

### Failure Cause Mapping

| If this behavior parameter value fails | Possible failure cause(s) |
|----------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| `samples_<N>` (basic `RESOLVE`) | Incorrect resolve mode for the format; wrong resolved value for a full/empty/partial mask; resolve attachment not written; image layout or copyback mistake |
| `samples_<N>_baseLayer1` | Resolve written to or read from the wrong array layer |
| `samples_<N>_resolve_level_<L>` | Resolve written to or read from the wrong mip level; mipmap offset calculation error in verification |
| `max_attachments_<P>_samples_<N>` | Resolve scaling failure at high attachment count; input-attachment / local-read read-back wrong image; subpass-to-subpass data flow broken |
| `compatibility_samples_<N>` | Implementation treated the two compatible render passes as incompatible, or resolve behaved differently across them |

### Cause Analysis

#### Incorrect resolve value for a mask pattern

**Possible failure symptoms:** for a given `m_sampleMask`, the resolved pixel does not match the expected result: clear value when the mask is empty, render value when the mask is full, or a value consistent across all color attachments for a partial mask. For float/fixed-point formats, the per-pixel average accumulated across all masks can also drift outside the format-dependent threshold. For integer formats, a partial mask can produce a value that is neither the clear value nor the render value, or whose components disagree.

**Possible implementation causes:** for float/fixed-point formats, this points to a resolve engine that does not correctly average the covered samples, for example always returning sample zero, or returning an uninitialised sample. For integer formats, it points to a resolve that does not return sample zero as required by `VK_RESOLVE_MODE_SAMPLE_ZERO_BIT`. The mask-cycling design exists to separate these cases: an empty mask must yield the clear value (no samples written), a full mask must yield the render value (all samples identical), and a partial mask must yield a value that is internally consistent and, for float/fixed-point, averages correctly over the full mask range.

#### Resolve written to or read from the wrong layer or level

**Possible failure symptoms:** the `baseLayer1` or `resolve_level_<L>` variant fails while the basic `samples_<N>` case for the same format and sample count passes; garbage or all-clear pixels appear in the copied-back buffer.

**Possible implementation causes:** the resolve targeted a different array layer or mip level than the one copied back to the host buffer. The test allocates a larger image and binds a specific layer/level view, so a mismatch between where the implementation wrote the resolved data and where the test read it produces this symptom. The source-level verification offset is computed from `m_renderLevel` and `m_baseLayer`, so a host-side miscalculation would also appear here, but that path is shared with the passing basic case and is therefore unlikely.

#### Resolve scaling failure at high attachment count

**Possible failure symptoms:** the `MAX_ATTACHMENTS` shape fails for a specific attachment count `P`, with the output attachments of subpass 1 deviating from the reference color `(0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.75)` beyond the format threshold; lower attachment counts for the same format pass.

**Possible implementation causes:** the implementation's on-chip resolve storage is exhausted or mis-managed when many color attachments resolve simultaneously, so one or more resolved images feeding subpass 1's input-attachment reads contain wrong data. Source comments describe this shape as testing "extreme cases where applications might consume all available on-chip memory." A failure here could also stem from input-attachment / `dynamic_rendering_local_read` plumbing that misroutes which resolved image is read by which binding, but that would tend to produce structured rather than threshold-exceeding deviations.

#### Compatible render passes diverged

**Possible failure symptoms:** the `COMPATIBILITY` case fails while the corresponding basic `samples_<N>` case passes; the resolved image produced when drawing against `m_renderPassCompatible` is incorrect, or the implementation rejects the framebuffer/pipeline created against `m_renderPass` as incompatible with `m_renderPassCompatible`.

**Possible implementation causes:** the implementation treated two render passes that the spec requires to be compatible as functionally different — either rejecting reuse of the framebuffer/pipeline, or selecting a different resolve path based on render-pass state that compatibility rules say must not affect behavior. The basic case proves resolve itself works for this format and sample count, so a compatibility-only failure isolates the divergence to render-pass-compatibility handling.

## Case Pruning

### Requirement-based pruning

Defined in [`checkSupport`](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L2996-L3071):

- `VK_KHR_maintenance5` is required for `VK_FORMAT_A8_UNORM_KHR`.
- `DEVICE_CORE_FEATURE_GEOMETRY_SHADER` is required when `layerCount > 1` (layered rendering via geometry shader).
- `VK_KHR_create_renderpass2` is required for the `renderpass2` path.
- `VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering` is required for the dynamic rendering path; `VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering_local_read` is additionally required for the `MAX_ATTACHMENTS` shape under dynamic rendering.
- `VK_KHR_portability_subset` `multisampleArrayImage` must be supported when combining multisampling with array images.
- `maxColorAttachments` and `maxPerStageDescriptorInputAttachments` limits are checked for the `MAX_ATTACHMENTS` shape.
- The format must support `VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT`, and the image must support the requested sample count, array layers, and extent.

### Design-based pruning

- `layerCount == 6` with `sampleCount == 8` is skipped because it is too slow ([source](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3838-L3840)).
- When a secondary command buffer is used, `sampleCount > 2` or `layerCount > 3` combinations are skipped to reduce test volume ([source](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassMultisampleResolveTests.cpp#L3842-L3844)).
- The `baseLayer1`, `resolve_level`, and `MAX_ATTACHMENTS`/`COMPATIBILITY` shapes are monolithic-pipeline-only or conditionally registered (see `## Behavior Parameters`); graphics pipeline library repeats only the `MAX_ATTACHMENTS` dynamic-rendering-local-read subset.

## Key Takeaways

- The resolve mode is determined by format channel class: `VK_RESOLVE_MODE_AVERAGE_BIT` for float and fixed-point, `VK_RESOLVE_MODE_SAMPLE_ZERO_BIT` for integer. The mask-cycling design exists to verify the correct mode is applied per format.
- An empty mask must resolve to the clear value and a full mask must resolve to the render value, for every format and sample count; partial masks must be internally consistent across all color attachments and, for float/fixed-point, must average to the expected midpoint over the full mask range.
- The `MAX_ATTACHMENTS` shape stresses on-chip resolve storage by resolving many attachments at once and feeding the results through a second subpass as input attachments; a failure isolated to high attachment counts points at resolve-scaling or input-attachment routing.
- `COMPATIBILITY` isolates render-pass-compatibility handling: the framebuffer/pipeline are created against a render pass with an unused resolve attachment and the draw is submitted against a compatible pass with a used resolve attachment. If the basic case passes but compatibility fails, the implementation treated the two compatible render passes as functionally different.
- The same logic is exercised across `renderpass1`, `renderpass2`, and dynamic rendering; non-monolithic pipelines and secondary command buffers reduce the sample/layer matrix, not the tested property.
